bottleneck: Depression involves disrupted circuits spanning prefrontal cortex, limbic system, and monoamine nuclei, but no circuit-level model predicts who responds to which treatment. Antidepressants, TMS, and ketamine all help subsets of patients for incompletely understood reasons, and treatment-resistant depression has no rational escalation path — clinicians cycle through options by trial and error. The field treats a circuit disorder without a circuit map, and diagnosis still rests on symptom checklists rather than biology.
current_state: Biomarker-guided treatment selection is experimental; psychiatry still relies on trial-and-error prescribing across drug classes, with each failed trial costing patients months.
title: Depression's causal circuits unmapped
why_it_blocks: The leading cause of disability worldwide is treated by guessing. Circuit-level understanding would turn psychiatry from art toward engineering, matching each patient to the intervention their brain actually needs.
